scope: Targeted check for deterministic chaos in the exact published reduced synchronematic model; not an exhaustive novelty certification.
checks: Main text and equations inspected. Supplementary PDF text searched throughout; relevant model/decomposition pages rendered and inspected. Peer review text checked. No explicit chaos or Lyapunov result for this model identified. The occurrence of Chaos in the supplement is a journal title in a citation, not a model result.

The author simulation repository source was inspected after our independent implementation and checks. A sign disagreement was found for the orientation sin(3 Delta) coefficient; source-audit.json pins the exact commit and records both variants. No author simulation source was copied or executed.

The OpenAlex snapshot returned one citing work, Particle-Induced Electroconvection in Nonpolar Liquids, doi:10.1021/acs.langmuir.6c02032. Its publisher abstract concerns EHD flow and self-assembly, not this phase-orientation chaos question.

Zhengyan Zhang 2023 dissertation downloaded from Columbia Academic Commons. Text searched throughout185pages; relevant Chapter3 and AppendixB pages read and rendered. Printed pp33-34 and FigB.3 p132 explicitly report single-particle chaos in the underlying charge-moment model. This is closer prior art than the 2005 inertial Quincke result.
known_related_chaos: Quincke rotor Lorenz chaos was reported in 2005: doi:10.1063/1.1827411. Broad Quincke-chaos novelty is excluded.
Self-propulsion in the 1D swarmalator model, arXiv:2606.10282, reports chaos in a different model. Broad swarmalator-chaos novelty is excluded.

Zhang2023 dissertation doi:10.7916/0pgk-pw45: single-particle strange attractor at Ee2.5,gamma1.2,eps_p1.5,kappa_p0; other nonsymmetric strange attractor at Ee6,gamma1. This excludes first-chaos claims for the underlying physical model.
limits: Only indexed/retrievable literature and the explicit sources above were checked. Equivalent equations under another name, dissertations, private/in-press work and missing citation-index records remain possible.
Our positive numerical evidence is for the noiseless fixed-position Fourier approximation. It is not proof for the full physical model or an experimental observation.
conclusion: A matching collective-chaos result for the exact reduced coupled phase/orientation equations was not located. Single-particle chaos in the underlying physical model is already reported. Any possible novelty is narrower and remains provisional.
